factors.name: Nasdaq-100
factors.rationale: The broad benchmark for large US tech and AI-exposed companies. A 25% fall from its 2-year high is a common bear-market yardstick.

factors.name: Semiconductors
factors.rationale: Semiconductors are a major AI-infrastructure exposure and can be sensitive to changes in technology-sector risk appetite.

factors.name: AI & tech ETF
factors.rationale: A basket of AI and big-data companies. It moves closely with the Nasdaq-100, so it carries a smaller weight.

factors.name: Data-center infrastructure ETF
factors.rationale: Data-center and digital-infrastructure companies: the physical AI build-out that much of the new debt is financing. Equity prices also reflect broader stock-market moves.

factors.name: BBB corporate spread (bp)
factors.rationale: Borrowing spreads on the lowest tier of investment-grade corporate debt, where much large-company and AI-related issuance prices.

factors.name: CCC high-yield spread (bp)
factors.rationale: Borrowing spreads on the riskiest rated corporate debt. It covers all CCC-rated borrowers rather than tech alone, but is a useful early-warning signal for vulnerable, highly leveraged companies.

factors.name: BDC (private credit) ETF
factors.rationale: Listed business development companies (BDCs), a market proxy for private credit, a major lender to growth and tech firms. Their share prices reflect credit concerns and broader stock-market moves.

factors.name: Leveraged loan ETF
factors.rationale: Leveraged loans: floating-rate funding for buyouts and below-investment-grade companies.

factors.name: High-yield spread (bp)
factors.rationale: The broad junk-bond spread, the market-wide gauge of credit stress.

changelog.note: Oracle and CoreWeave replaced by the data-center ETF, BBB and CCC spreads; dividend-adjusted prices; spread widening test; 2-year highs.
Financing Strain alert can also trigger on CCC spreads; stale-data flags.
Wording and disclosure updates only; no change to scores.

Exit rule: alerts pause in recovery mode, when the Nasdaq-100 is 20% or more above its lowest close since its 2-year high (start dates, including the implosion date, never move). New shock flag for an index of 60+ before any alert has confirmed. Index shown with its range under thresholds 20% tighter/looser. Backtest now judges every alert by one rule, is labelled in-sample, and keeps an out-of-sample record from 16 Oct 2026. Alert start triggers, thresholds and weights unchanged.

model.note: Every run recalculates the full history under the current version. Thresholds were shaped on the same history the backtest replays, so the backtest is in-sample; only alerts after the out-of-sample date are a true test.
